studies.label: Lab experiment: chatbot-avatar sketching with no support, Google Image Search, or Midjourney V4

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.2 (experiment sample); PDF p. 1, Abstract (experiment N); PDF p. 6, Section 3.3 (random assignment)
counts_source.quote: We recruited 60 participants through digital student notice boards, mailing lists of university student clubs, and word of mouth.

arms.name: GenAI
arms.description: Access to paid Midjourney V4 through a private Discord server, with a tool tutorial, to generate inspiration images while sketching. PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF p. 6, Section 3.3.

arms.name: Image Search
arms.description: Access to Google Images in an incognito browser, with a tool tutorial, for inspiration while sketching. PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF p. 6, Section 3.3.

arms.name: Baseline (No support)
arms.description: No inspiration-support tool; the same design brief, example avatar, materials, and task duration as the other conditions. PDF p. 4, Section 3.1.

studies.task: Sketch as many different chatbot-avatar ideas as possible on paper in 20 minutes after viewing a common example avatar intended to induce fixation (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1).

ai_tool.name: Midjourney V4 (paid version; Midjourney bot on a private Discord server)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3.1. May 2023 is the study date; the model release year is not stated.

estimates.outcome: Design fixation score: features of the example repeated in each sketch (condition effect)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two HCI researchers with experience teaching and evaluating design counted example features in each sketch. DFS is the number of repeated features divided by the example’s 14 salient features. The fitted binomial model uses the feature count and a probit link. Raters were blind to the experiment’s aims; the paper does not explain whether their counts were combined before modelling. PDF pp. 4-5, Section 3.1; PDF p. 7, Section 3.4; PDF p. 8, Section 4.2.

regression.model: Bayesian binomial regression of repeated example features on Inspiration Stimulus, with a probit link and random intercepts for participant and image. Baseline is the reference condition. Posterior SD as printed: 0.13. This is posterior dispersion of the coefficient, not an outcome SD or a frequentist standard error.

estimates.notes: The coefficient and interval are transcribed from the table. The interval is an 89% Bayesian compatibility (credible) interval, not a frequentist confidence interval. ci_of=difference denotes the GenAI-versus-Baseline coefficient on the model scale; outcome_scale=raw means unstandardized, without inverting the link. The parenthesized posterior SD is preserved verbatim in regression.model and the table quote. It is not entered as a regression SE or an outcome SD. test.type=other identifies the printed Bayes factor; no p-value or standardized effect is reported. se_basis=participant describes the model observation structure: participant random effects for sketch-level models, or one count per participant. The paper prints no analysis-specific participant counts or contrast-specific output count. Arm predictions and their error bars have no printed values and were not digitized. Design fixation remains construct=other: it scores copying of the supplied example, rather than novelty itself or diversity across people. Higher values mean greater fixation. The text gives an upper interval endpoint different from Table 1; the structured interval follows the table.

estimates.outcome: Variety: number of clusters covered by a participant’s sketches (total effects)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two raters blind to condition grouped sketches into 83 mutually exclusive clusters. The normalized score is (clusters covered by a participant minus one)/(total clusters minus one). The negative binomial model instead uses the number of clusters covered minus one, with a log link. The direct-effect model additionally adjusts for Fluency. This is variety within a participant, coded flexibility. PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, Equation 3; PDF p. 9, Section 4.4 and Table 3.

regression.model: Bayesian negative binomial regression of the number of clusters covered minus one on Inspiration Stimulus, with a log link. Total-effects specification without Fluency. Baseline is the reference condition. Posterior SD as printed: -.28. This is posterior dispersion of the coefficient, not an outcome SD or a frequentist standard error.

estimates.outcome: Originality: proportion of other participants without an idea in the sketch’s cluster (total effects)
estimates.question: with_ai

open_items: The experiment sample is printed, but no creativity model supplies its analyzed participant N or arm-specific analyzed Ns. Explicit total arm counts and two-arm participant totals are not printed. Equal allocation and gender-specific counts are not converted into totals; degrees of freedom and prompt counts are not used to infer participant counts.

No observed arm mean, participant-level outcome SD, output-level outcome SD, or standardized creativity effect is printed. Arm predictions and standard-error bars are figure-only. The GenAI sketch corpus total is not a per-participant mean.

Tables report posterior SDs and Bayesian compatibility intervals. The posterior SDs are preserved in regression.model and source quotes because the schema has no posterior-SD field. A null regression.se does not mean that Bayesian uncertainty is absent; the reported intervals are retained without conversion.
Table 3 prints a negative posterior SD for the GenAI total effect on Variety. Its sign is preserved verbatim in the model description and quote, but a usable posterior SD requires clarification.

Several results-text intervals disagree with their tables. The extraction consistently uses the table cells. The conclusion also conflicts with the total-effect ordering of GenAI and Image Search for Fluency and Variety.
No numerical GenAI-versus-Image-Search contrast or its uncertainty is printed for any eligible outcome. Shared-baseline coefficients are not subtracted.

The screening form flags unresolved fluency-response coding and variety-figure normalization. The PDF describes Fluency as sketch count and the Variety model response as clusters covered minus one. No shifted sketch count, digitized arm level, or transformation of the printed coefficients is assumed.

The design-fixation model includes participant and image random effects, but the paper does not specify whether the two raters’ counts were combined before modeling or give the model observation count. Output remains the stated scoring unit.

Originality refers to rarity of a sketch among other participants, but the paper does not explicitly delimit that reference pool by condition. This does not establish a separate within-arm diversity outcome.

The external study protocol mentioned in Section 3.1 is not in the saved PDF and has no printed retrieval URL. The randomization method beyond random assignment, including how gender balance was obtained, is not specified.
The study country and Midjourney V4 release year are not stated. Author affiliations and the study date are not substituted for these fields.
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-10 using both independent extractions, the supplied diff, the screening form and citation record, and the saved arXiv PDF. The entire markdown conversion, including references and Appendix A, was read in consecutive chunks. Every cited numerical table and page was checked with PyMuPDF page text. The saved version is the source of record; no external supplement, data, API, or web source was used. All four screening-form outcomes and both GenAI comparisons for each outcome are represented. No additional eligible outcome or contrast was found. Both extractors included direct-effect models adjusted for post-assignment variables; all three such records are removed and listed in not_extracted under extraction rule 5. There were no estimates unique to one extractor in the supplied diff. n_added is zero. Participants were randomized individually between conditions. Clusters used to score sketches are outcome categories, not assignment clusters. Only the experiment cohort is recorded as n_randomized; analysis-specific counts remain null. PDF p. 5 states: "Each condition had an equal number of participants and was gender-balanced, with 10 women and 10 men per condition (gender was self-described by participants)." PDF p. 5, Section 3.1 identifies "all the sketches (N=277)" and states "The process resulted in 83 clusters." These corpus/category totals are not contrast-specific observation counts. The GenAI sketch total is preserved in the fluency source quotes without division. No plotted, back-transformed, or computed value from the screening form was imported. All scored outputs were produced during the assigned task with the assigned tool available; no after_ai outcome is reported. Design fixation is coded other, Variety is flexibility, and Originality is novelty; none is recast as across_people diversity. Shared samples and preregistration are not reported. Numeric source quotes preserve printed precision and signs. Bayesian posterior SDs are not relabeled as frequentist SEs or as outcome SDs.
